newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans $1.3 bln Eurobonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans $1.3 bln Eurobonds in 1997.

text.p: Russia plans to issue $1.3 billion of Eurobonds in 1997, according to a copy of the 1997 draft budget obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
Listing other foreign borrowing planned by Russia in 1997, the draft said Moscow would raise
- $4.3 billion in untied credits from international financial organisations,
- $1.0 billion in untied credits from foreign governments, banks and companies,
- $1.9 billion in tied export credits, and
- $0.6 billion in tied credits from international financial organisations.
The draft, prepared on August 22, said total external borrowing would cover 40.6 trillion roubles of a planned 89.1 trillion rouble deficit, which is 3.3 percent of gross domestic product.
But a revised draft submitted to parliament on Monday put the overall deficit at 90.7 trillion roubles, which was still 3.3 percent of GDP.
Russian officials say Russia will make a first issue of $300-500 million of Eurobonds later this year.
Russia has mandated JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to manage the issue, and officials say the first bond could be presented at the end of September or early in October.
But a bond is unlikely to be launched until Russia has closed its $35 billion commercial bank debt rescheduling, and won a debt rating.
